'''''Quercus lusitanica''''', commonly known as '''gall oak''', '''Lusitanian oak''', or '''dyer's oak''', is a species of oak native to [[Portugal]], [[Spain]] ([[Galicia (Spain)|Galicia]] and western [[Andalucia]]) and [[Morocco]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://wcsp.science.kew.org/namedetail.do?name_id=173732 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190515044632/https://wcsp.science.kew.org/namedetail.do?name_id=173732 |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 15, 2019 |title=''Quercus lusitanica'' |work=[[World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]] (WCSP) |publisher=[[Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew]] }}</ref> ''Quercus lusitanica'' is the source of commercial nutgalls. These [[gall]]s are produced by the infection from the insect ''[[Cynips gallae tinctoriae]]''. They are used for [[dyeing]].

Several other species are known colloquially as "gall oaks;"  indeed, galls can be found on a large percentage of oak species.<ref name=cranshaw>{{cite book|last=Cranshaw|first=Whitney|title=Garden Insects of North America|url=https://archive.org/details/gardeninsectsofn0000cran|url-access=registration|year=2004|publisher=Princeton University Press|location=Princeton, New Jersey|isbn=0-691-09560-4}}</ref> The specific epithet "''lusitanica''" refers to the ancient Roman Province of [[Lusitania (Roman province)|Lusitania]], corresponding roughly to present-day Portugal and [[Extremadura]] in Spain.<ref name="hdp">{{cite book |title=História de Portugal: Uma Visão Global |last=Garcia |first=José Manuel |year=1989 |publisher=Editorial Presença |location= Lisboa|isbn=972-23-0989-7 |pages=32, 33, 38}}</ref>

==Description==
[[File:Quercus Lusitanica.jpg|thumb|left|''Quercus lusitanica'']]
''Quercus lusitanica'' is a stoloniferous shrub, usually prostrate, under 3 m in height.<ref name="iberica">{{cite web |title=Quercus lusitanica |url=http://www.floraiberica.es/floraiberica/texto/pdfs/02_041_03_Quercus.pdf |publisher=[[Flora Iberica]] |access-date=20 January 2021}}</ref>

== Taxonomy ==
It was incorrectly named ''Q. humilis'', later ''Q. fruticosa'' and its current name was incorrectly used to identify other Gall oaks from the Iberian Peninsula and North Africa. This resulted in numerous taxonomy errors in the Gall oaks taxa from the occidental and oriental [[Mediterranean Basin]].<ref name="iucn status 19 November 2021" />

==Distribution and habitat==
''Quercus lusitanica'' is native to the [[Iberian Peninsula]] (in Portugal and western [[Andalusia]], Spain, also rare on [[Galicia (Spain)|Galicia]]) and Morocco<ref name="iberica">{{cite web |title=Quercus lusitanica |url=http://www.floraiberica.es/floraiberica/texto/pdfs/02_041_03_Quercus.pdf |publisher=[[Flora Iberica]] |access-date=20 January 2021}}</ref> It is commonly associated in oak and pine forests and does well in acidic soils.<ref name="iucn status 19 November 2021" /> It favors mild coastal [[Mediterranean climate]]s but it also succeeds in moist, mild, [[maritime climate]]s.<ref name="temperateferns" /><ref name="flora-on">{{cite web |title=Quercus lusitanica Lam. |url=https://flora-on.pt/#/0e7nb |access-date=21 January 2021 |publisher=Flora-on}}</ref> It is relatively sensitive to cold temperatures<ref name="iucn status 19 November 2021" /> and is hardy down to {{convert|-8|C}}.<ref name="temperateferns">{{cite web |title=Quercus lusitanica |url=http://temperate.theferns.info/plant/Quercus+lusitanica |publisher=Temperate Plants Database, Ken Fern |access-date=20 January 2021}}</ref> It inhabits sandy or gravelly soils up to {{convert|600|m|ft|abbr=on}} in elevation.<ref name="iberica" /><ref>{{Cite iucn |title=''Quercus lusitanica'' |author=Harvey-Brown, Y. |name-list-style=amp |article-number=e.T79914375A79914412 |date=2017 |access-date=20 January 2021}}</ref>

==Threats==
No serious threats were found in Portugal, though in Andalusia this plant has been listed as [[Near Threatened]] due to fires, silviculture and grazing [[ungulate]]s.<ref name="iucn status 19 November 2021" /> The main threat to the conservation of genetic diversity of this species is the hybridization with the oak neighbors ([[Quercus rotundifolia|Holm Oak]], [[Cork Oak]], [[Kermes Oak]], [[Pyrenean Oak]]).<ref name="iucn status 19 November 2021" />
